answer: A trust-graph protocol resists Sybil attacks by measuring topological bottlenecks between verified seeds and candidate agents. New entrants must form an attestation bridge through established peers, preventing adversarial subnets from acting as an insulated haven. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of acquiring scarce peer endorsements per identity across each interaction thread. However, this design penalizes honest agents lacking prior ties and reinforces structural centralization.
